email.title: Email
email.intro: Forward your support mailbox to this address, and customer emails arrive here as tickets.
email.introDirect: Customer emails to this mailbox arrive here as tickets. It receives mail directly, so there is nothing to forward.
email.notConfigured: Email intake is not available for this workspace yet.
email.waiting: Waiting for your first forwarded email
email.waitingHint: Once forwarding is set up, send a test email to your support mailbox. When it arrives as a ticket, this shows Working. Select Refresh to check.
email.waitingDirect: Send a test email to {address}. When it arrives as a ticket, this shows Working. Select Refresh to check.
email.howTo: Set up an auto-forward from your support mailbox
email.gmail1: On a computer, open Gmail, select Settings and then See all settings.
email.gmail2: Open Forwarding and POP/IMAP, select Add a forwarding address and paste the address above.
email.gmail3: Gmail sends a confirmation message to that address. It should appear here as a new ticket. Open the link in it to confirm.
email.gmail4: Back in Forwarding and POP/IMAP, choose Forward a copy of incoming mail, pick the address, keep Gmail's copy in the inbox and select Save Changes.
email.outlook1: In Outlook on the web, open Settings, then Mail, then Forwarding.
email.outlook2: Turn on forwarding and paste the address above.
email.outlook3: Tick Keep a copy of forwarded messages and save.
email.outlook4: On Microsoft 365, your admin may first need to allow forwarding to outside addresses.
email.cpanel1: In cPanel, open Email and then Forwarders.
email.cpanel2: Select Add Forwarder and enter the address your customers write to.
email.cpanel3: Choose Forward to email address, paste the address above and select Add Forwarder.
email.newMailOnly: Forwarding copies new mail only. Messages already in the mailbox do not become tickets.
email.replies: Replies to customers go out from the platform. Customers reply to the ticket email as they would to any message, and their answer joins the same ticket.

whatsapp.autoTicketOn: On: a message that is not part of an open ticket opens a new one.
whatsapp.autoTicketOff: Off: only messages on an already open ticket are added.

widget.title: Web widget
widget.intro: Add a help button to your own website. Visitors open a small form, confirm their email with a code and send you a ticket without leaving the page.
widget.step2: Paste it into your website's HTML just before the closing </body> tag, on every page that should show the button. On WordPress, Wix or Shopify, use the theme's custom code or footer scripts setting.
widget.step3: Publish the page. A round help button appears in the bottom corner.
widget.optionsTitle: Optional settings on the script tag
widget.optionTheme: data-theme="light" or "dark" fixes the colours. Without it the form follows the visitor's device.
widget.optionPosition: data-position="left" puts the button on the left. It sits on the right by default.
widget.optionLabel: data-label="Need help?" sets the button's tooltip and the name screen readers announce.
widget.optionColor: data-color="#0f766e" sets the button colour to match your brand.
widget.preview: Open the widget form in a new tab
